successors.name: Burgundian State
successors.text: the county, bought in 1421 by Philip the Good: 'Philip became count of Namur on John's death in 1429'

ledger.x: About 990: the County of Namur appears.
1256: Henry V of Luxembourg seizes Namur.
ledger.cpn: County and Duchy of Luxembourg (House of Luxembourg)
County and Duchy of Luxembourg (House of Luxembourg)

ledger.x: 1264: Guy of Dampierre becomes Marquis of Namur.
1305: Namur leaves the count of Flanders.
1429: Philip the Good takes the county.

wars.name: Henry V of Luxembourg's seizure of Namur
wars.outcome: Baldwin II sold his rights to Guy of Flanders, who retook the margraviate from Henry in 1264; Henry and Guy made peace (Guy married Henry's daughter Isabelle).

certainty.note: No page gives a frontier for the county; the Province of Namur is a modern stand-in for the lands of the counts.
